# Hexgrids, specifically H3

![](../img/hexgrids.png)




## Square grids {style="font-size:0.7em"}

+ Conceptually simple

+ Multiple sets of coefficients needed for analysis due to edge neighbors and node neighbors
    + Four neighbors share an edge with the focal cell
    + Four additional neighbors touch only at a corner (node)
    + Edge and node neighbors are different distances from the focal cell's center
    + Analyses must therefore distinguish between edge-only (rook) and edge-plus-node (bishop) neighborhoods

```{=html}
<div style="text-align: center;">
  <video id="dymaxion-animation" controls loop muted playsinline preload="metadata"
         style="display: block; max-width: 90%; max-height: 52vh; width: auto; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; object-fit: contain;">
    <source src="https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9e/Dymaxion_2003_animation_remastered.webm"
            type="video/webm">
    Your browser does not support embedded WebM video.
  </video>
</div>
<script>
window.addEventListener("load", function () {
  const video = document.getElementById("dymaxion-animation");

  if (!video || typeof Reveal === "undefined") return;

  const fragment = video.closest(".fragment");

  function syncPlayback() {
    const currentSlide = Reveal.getCurrentSlide();
    const isVisible = fragment.classList.contains("visible");
    const isOnCurrentSlide = currentSlide && currentSlide.contains(video);

    if (isVisible && isOnCurrentSlide) {
      if (video.paused) {
        video.currentTime = 0;
        video.play().catch(function () {});
      }
    } else {
      video.pause();
      video.currentTime = 0;
    }
  }

  const observer = new MutationObserver(syncPlayback);
  observer.observe(fragment, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ["class"] });

  Reveal.on("slidechanged", syncPlayback);
  syncPlayback();
});
</script>
```

Animation by [Annaaurora](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:Annaaurora), based on Chris Rywalt's *Dymaxion Projection Animation* and NASA's *Blue Marble: Next Generation* imagery. ::: {.fragment .absolute .fade-in-then-out data-fragment-index="6"}

**A gnomonic icosahedral projection is neither equal-area, equidistant, nor conformal**.

- Areas become increasingly exaggerated away from each triangular face’s center.
- Angles and local shapes are not preserved, except approximately near each face’s tangency point.
- Great-circle routes project as straight lines within each face.
- Dividing the globe among 20 faces _limits_ the extent of distortion but does not eliminate it.

:::

:::

##  H3 {style="font-size:0.7em"}

+ __H3__ is an open source Hexagonal Hierarchical Spatial Index that was developed by Uber.
+ H3 uses gnomonic icosahedral projection, but...
+ it does not unfold the icosohedron to make a map,
+ rather it lays a hexagonal grid on the surface of the faces themselves forming a _geodesic discrete global grid system_

## Geodesic Discrete Global Grid System {style="font-size:0.7em"}
::: { .r-stack}

::: {.fragment .absolute .fade-out data-fragment-index="1"}
What?
:::

::: {.fragment .absolute .fade-in-then-out data-fragment-index="1"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
+ __Geodesic__ 
  - constructed on an approximation of the earth surface, rather than a plane.
  - “geodesic” describes its recursively subdivided icosahedral structure resembling the geometry used in Buckminster Fuller’s geodesic domes
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/Biosphere_montreal.JPG/960px-Biosphere_montreal.JPG){fig-alt="The geodesic dome of the Montreal Biosphere" style="display: block; max-width: 100%; max-height: 42vh; width: auto; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; object-fit: contain;"}

## Demonstration: Building damage hotspots {style="font-size:0.7em"}

**Question:** Where was building destruction concentrated?

1. Assign each assessed building to an H3 cell.
2. Count assessed and destroyed buildings in each cell.
3. Map the percentage destroyed.
4. Repeat at adjacent H3 resolutions.

$$
\text{percent destroyed} =
100 \times \frac{\text{destroyed buildings}}{\text{assessed buildings}}
$$

[Open the building-damage demonstration](https://kulpojke.github.io/damage-map-web-map/)

## What does H3 add? {style="font-size:0.7em"}

+ A geographic identifier replaces a repeated point-in-polygon spatial join.
+ The same workflow works at different resolutions.
+ Each cell has a consistent neighborhood for local comparisons.

**Note to self:** a cell with 1 destroyed building out of 1 assessed building is not
equivalent to a cell with 100 out of 100. Show the fraction and
suppress or flag cells with small sample sizes.
